# Napkin principles, ranked

Higher wins when two pull against each other (comitatus principle 01). From William's answers, by Elo.

| # | Rating | Compared | Principle | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1016 | 1 | Napkin G04 | Relationships stay live: copies, arrays, mirrors and fits follow later edits, and you can detach one on purpose. |
| 2 | 1016 | 1 | Napkin G06 | Typed values follow what you're doing: the direction you drag, and the model's units for a bare number; any unit you type, written however you write it, is understood. |
| 3 | 1016 | 1 | Napkin G09 | Never lose work: always saved, atomically, and undo crosses sessions without hiding changes made in FreeCAD. |
| 4 | 1016 | 1 | Napkin G10 | A rejected action says why and leaves nothing behind. |
| 5 | 1000 | 0 | Napkin G02 | The .FCStd file is the model: every action becomes ordinary, editable FreeCAD features, and Shop Sketch is a view of them. |
| 6 | 1000 | 0 | Napkin G03 | Work as SketchUp does, and as a Mac app does, unless there's a reason not to; a decision that departs from SketchUp says why. |
| 7 | 1000 | 0 | Napkin G05 | One key per idea, meaning the same thing in every tool. |
| 8 | 1000 | 0 | Napkin G07 | One meaning per colour: violet cuts, red rejects, amber is new; nothing else uses them except the red/green/blue axis guides. |
| 9 | 1000 | 0 | Napkin G11 | Nothing rests on memory: every decision is logged, every behaviour has a named test, and every prediction of FreeCAD's answer is checked against FreeCAD. |
| 10 | 984 | 1 | Napkin G01 | Feel first: a draft appears the moment you act and input never waits on FreeCAD; FreeCAD catches up and the wave confirms it. |
| 11 | 984 | 1 | Napkin G08 | Refer to geometry, never to FreeCAD's internal numbers. |
| 12 | 984 | 1 | Napkin G12 | Work splits by files, and one integrator merges, numbers and keeps the records. |
| 13 | 984 | 1 | Napkin G13 | Show what an edit will change before it does. |
